title: response-orchestration-playpen
content:
Purpose / quick note to self:
- Sketching a lightweight response orchestration layer for multi-model responses: combine generator + reranker + small-tool (search/QA) into a single flow with per-segment cost/latency controls.
- Goal: improve average answer precision for customer-facing assistants while keeping p50 latency <= 300ms for short queries and p95 <= 800ms.

Problem context:
- Many apps stitch multiple model calls downstream (candidate gen -> ranker -> finalizer). Each call adds tail latency and token cost. Hard to reason about economics at product level.
- We already have routing and fallback primitives. Need a small, embeddable "orchestrator" primitive that teams can configure per-route.

Core idea (high level):
- Response conductor: declarative small graph: nodes = {generator, re-ranker, tool-invocation, post-processor}. Edges annotated with policy: {latency_budget_ms, cost_budget_tokens, quality_guardrails}.
- Runtime will execute nodes in phases: fast-path parallel gen (cheap model), then optional rank, then selective re-gen / tool call for top-K only. Use KV/prefix cache to short-circuit repeated contexts.

User stories (rough):
- As an app developer, I want to define an orchestration json per route so I can trade off latency vs. precision without changing code.
- As SRE, I want to see token-level breakdown per node to identify hotspots.
- As product manager, I want a mode that favors lower cost for background tasks (async fallback) but high-precision for sync route.

API sketch / example snippet (pseudo config):
- route: /assistant/answer
- nodes:
  - id: genA, model: distil-gen, max_tokens: 120, budget_ms: 200
  - id: rank1, model: light-ranker, type: score, budget_ms: 80, inputs: [genA]
  - id: toolSearch, type: tool, selector: if rank1.top_score < 0.6, budget_ms: 300
  - id: finalizer, model: high-fidelity, condition: (rank1.top_k includes truthy)

Acceptance notes / metrics to watch:
- p50 latency, p95 latency (per route)
- token cost per successful answer (mean)
- fraction of queries that hit toolSearch (should be tunable)
- quality delta vs baseline gen-only (A/B using holdout set)

Open questions / risks:
- How to expose policy primitives without confusing product teams? Too many knobs. Maybe offer three profiles: lean, balanced, deep.
- Billing model: show estimated token cost during config; but runtime deviations happen. Provide sampling-based overage estimates.
- Cache invalidation semantics across orchestrator runs (prefix reuse across nodes).
- Can we rely on existing fallback routing to avoid duplicated effort? Need to map orchestrator states to global routing fallback hooks.

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Week 1: prototype orchestrator as a thin controller in hosted API layer that issues up to 2 generator calls + 1 ranker. No fancy caching, just orchestration logic.
- Week 2: run synthetic workload (100k queries) using stored prompt set: measure latency and token cost.
- Week 3: small internal beta (SSO internal) tied to feature flag, collect telemetry and failure cases.

Nice-to-have features later:
- Graph UI in Console to draw node flows and tune budgets visually.
- Offline optimizer that suggests node budgets for target SLO/cost objective.
- Auto-fallback to cheaper generator during peak or degraded hardware.

To-do / action items (personal):
- Pull sample prompts from customer-llm-evals (JIRA INF-6721).
- Sync with infra on tracing hooks (instrument per-node token/latency).
- Draft small proto PR (repo: orch-proto) to show basic config -> runtime mapping.

Notes to self (brainlet):
- Keep first MVP minimal: generator + ranker, single conditional tool call. Avoid exposing dozens of policy knobs.
- Emphasize telemetry, that's how we sell it to PMs and SREs.
- Consider offering template presets: faq-answering, creative-assistant, data-aware-qa.

Random ideas thrown in while brainstorming:
- 'staged commitments' where we return a partial answer fast and continue improving in background (useful for mobile).
- credit-based per-route budgets visible in Console (quota tokens dedicated to a route).

End-of-file notes: still rough. Next step: pair with Mika to sketch runtime API and Jordan to validate metrics in Console.
